startup.task_failed: A background service could not start: {0}
firstrun.title: Welcome to TM Publisher
firstrun.intro: TM Publisher keeps everything in an encrypted database on this computer. Start fresh, or bring your data from a backup file.
firstrun.restore.hint: Brings accounts, groups, posts and settings from a .tmpbak file.
firstrun.protection.keyring: The database key is protected by this computer's keyring and opens automatically when you sign in.
firstrun.protection.nokeyring: No keyring was found on this computer: the database is protected with a master password that is asked at every start.
firstrun.use_master_password: Ask for a master password at every start instead
password.too_short: The password must be at least {0} characters.
password.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
password.forgotten_warning: If you forget this password, the data cannot be recovered by anyone.
unlock.title: Open TM Publisher
unlock.automatic_failed: The database key could not be opened automatically: {0}
restore.missing: Choose a backup file and type its password.
restore.wrong_password: The backup password is wrong, or the file is damaged.
restore.missing_files: Backup restored. {0} media files of unsent posts are not on this computer: {1}
restore.explain: Restoring replaces the current data with the backup (the current database is kept aside in the data folder).
restore.master_password_note: Switch to the keyring protection first, then restore; you can set the master password again afterwards.
backup.explain: A backup contains the encrypted database only (accounts, keys, groups, posts, settings), not your media files. A forgotten backup password cannot be recovered.
settings.notifications: Show notifications in the bottom-right corner
settings.notification_seconds: Keep a notification on screen for (seconds)
settings.autostart: Start with my computer (in the tray)
settings.tiktok_draft: Send TikTok posts as drafts to the TikTok inbox by default
settings.saved_restart: Saved. The new language applies after a restart.
settings.protection.keyring: The database key is protected by this computer's keyring.
settings.protection.password: The database key is protected by your master password.
settings.license: Free and open source under the MIT license. Third-party notices are in the licenses folder next to the app.
accounts.intro: Every account is connected with your own developer app or key; TM Publisher has no shared app and no server.
accounts.empty: No account yet. Add one to start.
account.state.reconnect: Connect again: the platform no longer accepts the key
account.state.reconnect_by: Connect again before {0} (the platform has no automatic renewal)
groups.intro: A group is a named list of accounts in sending order. A post goes to a group or to accounts you pick; never to nobody.
groups.name: Group name
groups.order_hint: Tick the members; the arrows set the sending order.
connect.title: Connect an account
connect.fill_required: Fill in every field marked with *.
connect.waiting_browser: Sign in in the browser window that opened; TM Publisher waits for the answer.
connect.registering: Registering your app on your server…
connect.paste_redirect: After signing in, the browser shows an error page or an empty page: copy the whole address from the address bar and paste it here.
connect.paste_code: Copy the code the page shows after you allow access, and paste it here.
field.redirect_uri: Return address (register exactly this in your app)
field.redirect_https: Return address registered in your app (https)
field.client_id: Client ID / App ID / Client key
field.chat_id.hint: @channelname for a public channel, or the numeric chat id (starts with -100 for channels and supergroups).
reason.no_mixed: {0} cannot mix photos and videos in one post.
field.mastodon_server.hint: For example mastodon.social: the address of the server your account is on.
guide.telegram.1: In Telegram open @BotFather, send /newbot and choose a name and a username; BotFather answers with a token.
guide.telegram.3: Add the bot to your channel or group as an administrator with the right to post messages.
guide.telegram.4: Write the channel's @username (public channel) or its numeric id into "Channel or group".
guide.telegram.5: Click "Connect and test": TM Publisher reads the bot and the channel.
warning.telegram.limits: Files up to 50 MB (photos 10 MB), captions up to 1,024 characters; Telegram's limit for bots.
guide.discord.1: In Discord open the channel's settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook (you need the Manage Webhooks right).
guide.discord.2: Give it a name and a picture, check the channel, then click "Copy Webhook URL".
guide.discord.4: Click "Connect and test": TM Publisher reads the webhook's name.
warning.discord.secret: Anyone with the webhook address can post to the channel: keep it secret (TM Publisher stores it encrypted).
warning.discord.limits: Up to 10 files, 20 MB each and 25 MB per post; text up to 2,000 characters.
guide.bluesky.1: In Bluesky open Settings → Privacy and security → App passwords → Add App Password. Never use your main password here.
guide.bluesky.2: Give it a name (for example "TM Publisher") and copy the generated password (xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx).
guide.bluesky.3: Write your handle and paste the app password.
guide.bluesky.4: Leave "Server" as https://bsky.social unless your account is on another server (PDS).
warning.bluesky.limits: Text up to 300 characters; up to 4 photos (2 MB each) or one video (50 MB). Links and hashtags are marked so they stay clickable.
guide.mastodon.1: Write the address of your server (for example mastodon.social).
guide.mastodon.2: Click "Connect and test": TM Publisher registers its own app on your server for your account (no approval needed) and opens the sign-in page.
guide.mastodon.3: Sign in if needed and click "Authorize"; the page shows a code.
guide.mastodon.4: Copy the code and paste it into the box that appears in this window.
warning.mastodon.limits: Limits come from your server; the usual ones are 500 characters and 4 attachments (photos or one video).
reason.youtube_video_only: {0} accepts videos only (community posts have no API).
guide.youtube.1: Create a project in Google Cloud (a free Google account is enough).
guide.youtube.2: Enable "YouTube Data API v3" in that project.
guide.youtube.3: Google Auth Platform → Branding: give the app a name and your e-mail address.
guide.youtube.4: Audience: choose "External" and click "Publish app" so it is "In production" (in "Testing" Google drops the access after 7 days).
guide.youtube.5: Clients → Create client → Application type "Desktop app"; copy the Client ID and the Client secret.
guide.youtube.6: Paste them here and click "Connect and test"; the browser opens Google's sign-in.
guide.youtube.7: Choose the account of the channel. Google shows "Google hasn't verified this app" for your own unverified app: click "Advanced" → "Go to … (unsafe)" — it is your app.
warning.youtube.private: YouTube may keep videos uploaded by an unaudited project private; if so, apply for the API audit in the Google Cloud project or change the visibility in YouTube Studio.
warning.youtube.quota: About 100 uploads per project per day; the quota resets at midnight Pacific Time.
warning.youtube.unverified: An unverified app can be used by up to 100 Google accounts: enough for you.
guide.x.1: Open the X developer console and sign in with the X account that will post.
guide.x.2: Create a Project and an App. In the app's "User authentication settings" choose OAuth 2.0, type "Native App", permissions "Read and write".
guide.x.3: Add this exact Callback URI (copy it) and any website address, then save.
guide.x.4: Copy the OAuth 2.0 Client ID (a native app has no secret).
guide.x.5: X is pay per use: add credits to the developer account before posting.
guide.x.6: Paste the Client ID and click "Connect and test"; allow access in the browser.
warning.x.cost: X charges per post (about $0.015; a post with a link about $0.20). The compose screen shows the estimate before sending.
reason.instagram_video_only: {0} takes only videos (Reels) in this version: photos must come from a public web address.
reason.threads_text_only: {0} takes only text in this version: photos and videos must come from a public web address.
field.meta_user_token: User access token from Graph API Explorer
field.meta_user_token.hint: Used once to get the Page's own token; it is not stored.
field.meta_page_id: Page ID (only if the token sees several Pages)
field.meta_page_id.hint: Leave empty when you manage one Page; TM Publisher lists the Pages it sees otherwise.
guide.facebook.1: On Meta for Developers create an app (use case "Other", type "Business"). It is your own app; it stays in development mode.
guide.facebook.2: App settings → Basic: copy the App ID and the App Secret.
guide.facebook.3: Open Graph API Explorer, pick your app, choose "Get User Access Token" and add pages_show_list, pages_read_engagement and pages_manage_posts.
guide.facebook.4: Click "Generate Access Token", choose your Page when Facebook asks, then copy the token.
guide.facebook.5: Paste the App ID, App Secret and token here and click "Connect and test": TM Publisher takes the Page's token, which does not expire.
warning.meta.devmode: Your app stays in development mode. Check once from another account that a test post is visible to others; if not, switch the app to Live (Meta may ask for a privacy policy address).
guide.instagram.1: Make the Instagram account a professional (Business or Creator) account and link it to a Facebook Page you manage.
guide.instagram.2: On Meta for Developers create an app (use case "Other", type "Business"); App settings → Basic: copy the App ID and App Secret.
guide.instagram.3: Add the "Instagram" product (API setup with Facebook Login) to the app.
guide.instagram.4: In Graph API Explorer get a user token with instagram_basic, instagram_content_publish, pages_show_list, pages_read_engagement and business_management.
guide.instagram.5: Choose the Page and the Instagram account when Facebook asks, then copy the token.
guide.instagram.6: Paste everything here and click "Connect and test".
warning.instagram.video_only: Videos (Reels) only in this version: Instagram takes photos only from a public web address.
warning.instagram.limits: 100 posts in 24 hours, at most 5 hashtags, caption up to 2,200 characters, video up to 300 MB.
guide.threads.1: On Meta for Developers create an app with the use case "Access the Threads API".
guide.threads.2: App roles → Roles → add your Threads account as a "Threads Tester", then accept the invite in Threads (Settings → Account → Website permissions).
guide.threads.3: Use cases → Threads API → Settings: add this return address to "Redirect Callback URLs" (copy it) and save.
guide.threads.4: Copy the Threads App ID and the Threads App Secret from the same page.
guide.threads.5: Paste them here and click "Connect and test"; allow access in the browser.
guide.threads.6: The browser then lands on an address that does not load: copy the whole address from the address bar and paste it into the box here.
warning.threads.text_only: Text only in this version: Threads takes photos and videos only from a public web address.
warning.threads.renewal: Access lasts 60 days and TM Publisher renews it when it is used; if the app is not used for that long, connect again.
reason.pinterest_media: {0} needs one photo or one video (a pin).
note.tiktok_approve: The video is in your TikTok inbox: open TikTok on your phone and finish the post from the notification.
note.tiktok_private: Posted privately (only you can see it): an unaudited TikTok app cannot post publicly. Change the visibility in the TikTok app.
field.linkedin_token: Access token from LinkedIn's token generator
field.pinterest_board: Board name or id (empty: your first board)
guide.tiktok.1: Sign in to TikTok for Developers and create an app (Manage apps → Connect an app).
guide.tiktok.2: Add the products "Login Kit" (platform: Desktop) and "Content Posting API"; turn on "Direct Post" if you want the private direct option.
guide.tiktok.3: In Login Kit add this exact redirect address (copy it).
guide.tiktok.4: Add the scopes user.info.basic, video.upload and video.publish; for a sandbox, add your TikTok account as a target user.
guide.tiktok.5: Copy the Client key and the Client secret.
guide.tiktok.6: Paste them here and click "Connect and test"; allow access in the browser.
warning.tiktok.drafts: By default the video goes to your TikTok inbox as a draft; you finish the post (caption, visibility) in the TikTok app. Drafts carry no text.
warning.tiktok.private: Direct posting is optional and, for an app that TikTok has not audited, always private (only you can see it).
warning.tiktok.audit: TikTok's audit does not accept "a tool to upload to my own accounts", so public direct posts stay closed; at most 5 drafts may wait in 24 hours.
guide.linkedin.1: Create an app on LinkedIn Developers (a LinkedIn Page is required as the app's company; your own page is fine).
guide.linkedin.2: Products: request "Share on LinkedIn" and "Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect" (both are granted at once).
guide.linkedin.3: Open the OAuth token generator, choose your app and the scopes openid, profile and w_member_social, then request the token.
guide.linkedin.4: Copy the access token and paste it here.
warning.linkedin.renew: The token lasts 60 days and LinkedIn does not let personal apps renew it automatically: connect again every 60 days (the account list reminds you a week before).
guide.pinterest.1: On Pinterest Developers connect your app (a business account is recommended).
guide.pinterest.2: Add this return address (copy it) to the app's redirect URIs. Any https address works; the page does not need to load.
guide.pinterest.3: Copy the App id and the App secret key.
guide.pinterest.4: Paste them here, optionally write the board, and click "Connect and test".
guide.pinterest.5: After allowing access the browser lands on an address that does not load: copy it from the address bar and paste it into the box here.
warning.pinterest.trial: With Trial access your pins are visible only to you. Standard access needs a short video showing the app's sign-in, sent to Pinterest for review.
warning.pinterest.business: Apps created on or after 14 September 2026 may get "403" for personal (non-business) accounts; use a business account.
